title: The 1911 Mona Lisa disappearance
hook: The Mona Lisa became the world's most famous painting partly by going missing.
peek: In August 1911 the Mona Lisa vanished from the Louvre, carried out by a handyman who had worked there. It was missing for over two years. The headlines turned a respected painting into the most famous picture on Earth.
lede: On a Monday in August 1911, when the Louvre was closed, an Italian handyman named Vincenzo Peruggia walked out with the Mona Lisa hidden under his work smock. He had helped fit glass cases in the museum. Nobody raised the alarm until the next day. The painting stayed missing for more than two years, and the world could not stop talking about it.

bullets.text: When the Louvre reopened, people queued to look at the bare hooks where the painting had hung. Newspapers around the world printed its face, making it famous far beyond art circles.
The poet Guillaume Apollinaire was briefly held, and Pablo Picasso was questioned, because of an earlier, unrelated affair involving statuettes taken from the Louvre. Both were cleared.

In 1913 Peruggia offered the painting to a Florence art dealer, who called in the director of the Uffizi Gallery. It was shown in Italy before going home to Paris. Peruggia said he wanted it returned to Italy, and he served only a short sentence.
A popular story says a con man had forgers make copies to sell as the stolen original. It comes from a 1932 magazine article, and historians doubt it happened.
